Plan a green corner

Imagine a small park entrance with room for one path, two planting beds, and one bench. Compare three ways to arrange them. Green World Park is credited to @gorayii in the historical inventory (page 15). These layouts come from the prototype exercise at the Community Office Garden; no separate Green World Park venue is built.

Compare the layouts

Direct path

A straight path keeps the crossing short. Place the bench in a side bay so a person stopping to rest does not block the route.

Loop around the beds

A loop lets visitors see both sides of the planting beds, but takes more path space. Leave room for people to pass at the bench.

Path along the edge

Keeping the path to one side leaves a larger planted area together. Orient the bench toward the beds and keep its approach out of the planting.

Make a choice and explain it

One visitor needs a short crossing; another wants to pause without blocking the way. Choose a layout. Say or sketch where its path, beds and bench go, and describe one compromise. Then choose again for someone who wants to see both sides of the beds.

Compare with one possible answer

A direct path suits a short crossing; a side bay makes room to rest. A loop offers more views of the beds but uses more of the same small space. Neither choice helps if the route to the bench is blocked.

To compare layouts in 3D, visit the Community Office Garden board and open Plan a green corner. This exercise does not change the park, award points, or record your choice.
